title: Mock 2 · Rules of the Game
blurb: Regulatory thresholds, structures and fund concepts, with one short caselet.

questions.q: Which of the following is explicitly EXCLUDED from the definition of an AIF under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations?
options: A privately pooled private equity fund
A privately pooled venture capital fund
questions.explanation: Family trusts, ESOP/employee benefit trusts, holding companies, securitisation SPVs, mutual funds, CIS and funds regulated by RBI or another regulator are excluded.
hints: Correct: ESOP and other employee benefit trusts are explicitly excluded.
Wrong: a privately pooled PE fund is a classic AIF (Category II).
Wrong: VC funds are Category I AIFs.
Wrong: infrastructure funds are Category I AIFs.

questions.q: The Corporate Debt Market Development Fund (CDMDF) is classified as which category of AIF?
options: It is not an AIF but a mutual fund scheme
questions.explanation: CDMDF is classified under Category I AIF as it is set up with the broader economic objective of developing the corporate bond market and acting as a backstop during market stress.
hints: Wrong: although it buys debt, it is placed in Category I.
Wrong: it does not use leverage or complex trading.
Wrong: it is a close-ended AIF formed as a trust.
Correct: CDMDF is classified under Category I because of its backstop purpose.

questions.q: If a scheme has total capital commitments of ₹1,000 crore and has drawn down ₹650 crore so far, the undrawn ₹350 crore is called:
questions.explanation: Invested capital is ₹650 crore against committed capital of ₹1,000 crore; the undrawn ₹350 crore is known as dry powder.
hints: Wrong: carry is the manager's profit share.
Correct: the undrawn committed amount is known as dry powder.
Wrong: hurdle is the preferred return.
Wrong: clawback recovers excess carry.

questions.q: In the international '2-20' fee structure for private equity funds, '20' refers to:
options: 20% additional return (carried interest) to the manager
questions.explanation: PE funds in developed markets have customarily been structured as '2-20': 2% management fee and 20% additional returns (carry).
hints: Wrong: hurdle is typically ~8% in developed markets.
Wrong: no such drawdown norm.
Wrong: not a tenure reference.
Correct: 2% management fee and 20% additional return.

questions.q: Category I and II AIFs may invest NOT more than what percentage of their investable funds in a single investee company?
questions.explanation: Category I and II AIFs shall invest not more than 25% of investable funds in one investee company directly or through units of other AIFs (LVFs up to 50%).
hints: Correct: 25% of investable funds.
Wrong: 10% relates to the borrowing limit.
Wrong: 50% applies only to large value funds for accredited investors.
Wrong: 15% is the associate-holding test, not this limit.

questions.q: A 'Large Value Fund for Accredited Investors' is one in which each investor (other than manager, sponsor, employees or directors) is an accredited investor investing at least:
questions.explanation: LVF means an AIF/scheme in which each investor (other than manager, sponsor, employees or directors) is an accredited investor and invests not less than ₹25 crore.
hints: Correct: minimum ₹25 crore per accredited investor.
Wrong: ₹70 crore is the PPM template/audit waiver ticket.
Wrong: ₹10 crore is the SSF minimum.
Wrong: ₹1 crore is the general minimum.

questions.q: Under FEMA, an individual is generally a 'person resident in India' if he/she resided in India for more than how many days during the preceding financial year (subject to intention tests)?
questions.explanation: Section 2(v) of FEMA: a person residing in India for more than 182 days during the preceding financial year, subject to intention-based exclusions.
hints: Correct: more than 182 days in the preceding financial year.
Wrong: not the FEMA threshold.
Wrong: not the FEMA threshold.
Wrong: not the FEMA threshold.

questions.q: In which AIF structure does the offshore fund invest its entire capital into the domestic SEBI-registered AIF rather than directly into investee companies?
questions.explanation: The unified structure is like the parallel one except the offshore fund makes no direct investments; its entire capital is invested into the domestic AIF.
hints: Wrong: in a parallel structure the offshore fund invests directly via FVCI/FDI.
Wrong: a pure offshore fund invests directly from abroad.
Wrong: a pure domestic fund has no offshore fund.
Correct: in a unified structure all offshore capital is routed through the domestic AIF.

questions.q: Which is a drawback of the LLP structure for an AIF compared with a trust?
options: LLPs cannot be registered as AIFs
LLPs cannot appoint an investment manager
Investor details come into the public domain and entry/exit of partners is cumbersome
questions.explanation: An LLP demands higher compliance; all investors become partners making entry/exit cumbersome, and as LLPs are regulated by MCA, investor details come into public domain.
hints: Wrong: partners' liability is limited to their agreed contribution.
Wrong: AIF Regulations allow LLP structures.
Wrong: an IMA is entered into with the manager.
Correct: LLPs are regulated by MCA and every investor becomes a partner.

questions.q: A bond with a 15% coupon pays interest half-yearly. What is its effective annual yield as per the workbook?
questions.explanation: Effective rate = (1 + k/m)^m − 1 = (1.075)^2 − 1 = 15.56%. Faster cash flows raise the yield.
hints: Wrong: this is annual payment.
Wrong: this is quarterly payment.
Wrong: this is monthly payment.

questions.q: The J-curve in AIF returns refers to:
options: Steadily rising returns from the first year
High returns early followed by a decline
Returns that track the stock market index exactly
Negative returns in early years due to fees and young investments, followed by rising returns as exits occur
questions.explanation: Cash flows are initially negative during the investment period due to fees and expenses; returns improve and turn positive once investments yield and are realised.
hints: Wrong: early years are typically negative.
Wrong: this is the reverse pattern.
Wrong: AIF returns are not index-tracking.
Correct: early negative cash flows, later positive as investments are realised.

questions.q: Which document qualifies the representations and warranties given by an investee company in the Share Subscription Agreement by listing specific exceptions?
questions.explanation: The Disclosure Letter serves as a formal qualifier to absolute R&Ws in the SSA; once a fact is disclosed, the AIF generally cannot later claim breach of warranty for it.
hints: Wrong: the PPM is the fund's offer document.
Wrong: the term sheet is a non-binding precursor.
Correct: the disclosure letter is the formal qualifier to R&Ws.
Wrong: the trust deed constitutes the AIF.

questions.q: Within how many calendar days must an AIF redress investor grievances under the SCORES framework?
questions.explanation: Based on the SEBI (Facilitation of Grievance Redressal Mechanism) amendment, AIFs shall redress investor grievances within 21 calendar days from the date of receipt.
hints: Wrong: not the prescribed timeline.
Wrong: not the prescribed timeline.
Correct: 21 calendar days from receipt.
Wrong: not the prescribed timeline.

questions.q: Why should an investor NOT rely solely on the fact that a reputed institution has committed capital to an AIF?
options: Every investor has specific outcomes and must do its own due diligence
Institutions are barred from investing in AIFs
Institutional commitments are not counted in the corpus
Institutions always get guaranteed returns through side letters
questions.explanation: Investors should not take comfort from the fact that a large institution has committed capital; every investor may have specific required outcomes from due diligence.
hints: Correct: the workbook warns against borrowed comfort from a large institution's commitment.
Wrong: institutions are major AIF investors.
Wrong: their commitments form part of the corpus.
Wrong: no AIF investor gets guaranteed returns.

questions.q: Which agencies have published AIF benchmarks after appointment by IVCA?
questions.explanation: Currently three benchmarking agencies appointed by IVCA (CRISIL, NSE and Preqin) publish AIF benchmarks for all categories, in USD and INR.
hints: Wrong: these are regulators/educators.
Wrong: not the named agencies.
Wrong: not the named agencies.
Correct: the three benchmarking agencies named in the workbook.

questions.q: A manager invests well above the mandatory minimum continuing interest in its own fund. From an investor's perspective this primarily signals:
options: That the fund is guaranteed to perform
That the manager will charge no fees
Greater 'skin in the game' and alignment of interests
That the fund will be listed
questions.explanation: Continuing interest provides 'skin in the game' for the manager; many first-time managers invest more than the minimum to give investors comfort.
hints: Wrong: no guarantee is implied.
Wrong: fees are unrelated to commitment.
Correct: continuing interest removes a main source of misalignment and moral hazard.
Wrong: listing is unrelated.

questions.q: In an AIF trust, investors are typically given which of the following to show their determinate share, rather than unit certificates?
questions.explanation: In the trust structure, unit certificates are not required, but a statement of account needs to be furnished to investors to show their determinate share.
hints: Wrong: shares are for companies.
Wrong: partnership deeds are for LLPs.
Correct: a statement of account is furnished to investors.
Wrong: unrelated instrument.

questions.q: Which statement about SEBI's role regarding an AIF's PPM is correct?
options: SEBI approves the PPM and guarantees its accuracy
SEBI drafts the PPM for the AIF
SEBI gives observations but does not approve the PPM
The PPM is never filed with SEBI
questions.explanation: SEBI provides only observations on the PPM and does not approve it; the disclaimer states SEBI assumes no responsibility for accuracy of disclosures.
hints: Wrong: the mandated disclaimer says the opposite.
Wrong: the manager and merchant banker are responsible.
Correct: submission to SEBI does not mean approval.
Wrong: PPMs are filed with SEBI.

questions.q: Under Regulation 27, the manager or sponsor must maintain records such as valuation policies and rationale for investments for how long?
options: 5 years after the winding up of the fund
3 years from the date of each investment
questions.explanation: All records under Regulation 27 are required to be maintained for a period of five years after the winding up of the fund.
hints: Correct: five years after winding up.
Wrong: not the prescribed period.
Wrong: not the prescribed period.
Wrong: records must outlive the fund.

questions.q: Using CAPM, what is the cost of equity if the risk-free rate is 7%, the market return is 13% and the company's beta is 1.5?
questions.explanation: Cost of equity = Rf + β × (ER − Rf) = 7% + 1.5 × 6% = 16%.
hints: Wrong: 1.5 × 13% is not the CAPM formula.
Wrong: that is just the market return.
Wrong: 1.5 × 7% ignores the market premium.

questions.q: At what rate must a Category I/II AIF deduct tax on income (other than business income) distributed to RESIDENT investors?
questions.explanation: As per section 393, an Investment Fund deducts tax at 10% on income (other than business income) distributed to resident investors.
hints: Wrong: 20% applies to dividends paid to non-residents.
Correct: 10% on all income other than business income.
Wrong: not the withholding rate.
Wrong: TDS is applicable.

questions.q: Based on the case, what is the MINIMUM continuing interest Raghav Capital must hold if the scheme closes at ₹200 crore?
questions.explanation: Continuing interest = lower of 2.5% of corpus (₹5 crore) or ₹5 crore = ₹5 crore.
hints: Wrong: 2.5% of ₹100 crore, not the corpus here.
Correct: 2.5% of ₹200 crore = ₹5 crore, which equals the cap, so ₹5 crore.
Wrong: 2.5% of ₹300 crore exceeds the ₹5 crore cap.
Wrong: arithmetic error.
questions.case: Raghav Capital is the sponsor and manager of 'Raghav Growth Fund', a SEBI-registered Category II AIF trust. The first scheme targets a corpus of ₹200 crore with a green-shoe option of ₹100 crore. Investors include HNIs, two employees of the manager, and a family office. The scheme has a 7-year tenure from first close. Raghav Capital plans to invest in later-stage unlisted consumer companies and wants to keep its own commitment as small as the regulations allow. A distributor, Meera, is pitching the scheme to her clients.

questions.q: If the green-shoe is fully subscribed and the corpus becomes ₹300 crore, the sponsor/manager commitment required will be:
questions.explanation: Lower of 2.5% × ₹300 crore (₹7.5 crore) and ₹5 crore = ₹5 crore.
hints: Wrong: ignores the 'whichever is lower' cap.
Correct: 2.5% would be ₹7.5 crore but the lower figure, ₹5 crore, applies.
Wrong: arithmetic error.
Wrong: ₹10 crore was the old Category III cap.

A distributor, Meera, is pitching the scheme to her clients.

questions.q: What is the minimum amount each of the two employees of the manager must invest if they participate in their individual capacity?
questions.explanation: Contribution of each employee or director of the fund or of the investment manager shall not be less than ₹25 lakh.
hints: Wrong: ₹1 crore applies to other investors.
Correct: employees/directors of the AIF or manager need at least ₹25 lakh.
Wrong: not a prescribed threshold.
Wrong: a minimum of ₹25 lakh applies.

The scheme has a 7-year tenure from first close. Raghav Capital plans to invest in later-stage unlisted consumer companies and wants to keep its own commitment as small as the regulations allow. A distributor, Meera, is pitching the scheme to her clients.

questions.q: While pitching the scheme, which statement by Meera would be a breach of distributor good practices?
options: 'Please read the PPM, especially the risk factors.'
'This scheme will definitely deliver at least 15% a year.'
'The management fee and carry are disclosed in the PPM.'
'The scheme is close-ended and illiquid for its 7-year tenure.'
questions.explanation: Distributors must abstain from indicating or assuring returns, unless it is a pure debt scheme with assured returns explicitly provided in the PPM.
hints: Wrong: urging investors to read the PPM is a good practice.
Correct: assuring returns in an equity AIF is prohibited.
Wrong: disclosing fees and carry is required.
Wrong: highlighting illiquidity is proper risk disclosure.
